concepts.gloss_en: the hidden/concealed aspect (bechinat nistar) — the singular quality of concealment, e.g. of Torah or of the 'legs' hidden in secret

members.note: singular abstract aspect of concealment, 'bechinat nistar'; cited with 'הנסתרות לה' but as the quality itself

concepts.gloss_en: hidden matters/things (plural) — the concealed elements, e.g. the words of Torah surrounding the mitzvah, that which is too elevated/hidden to act upon

members.note: plural 'hidden things' denoting specific concealed matters (dibburim around the mitzvah; the elevated/inaccessible). Distinct number and referent from singular abstract נסתר; under-merge preferred

notes: Singular נסתר names the quality/aspect of concealment; plural נסתרות names discrete hidden matters. Both from Likutey Moharan I, overlapping in lm1:22, but the number difference tracks a real referential difference (aspect vs. things). Kept separate per under-merge rule; reviewer may consider them two grammatical faces of one concept.
